data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The fetch budget must be denominated in both requests and bytes, and exhaustion must be recorded as a typed terminal state that includes a full audit log of every fetch attempt (including retries) to ensure complete reproducibility. This eliminates single-denomination rivals because only a dual log can capture the causal chain of exhaustion.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log grows too large, it could itself become a resource drain and introduce non-determinism due to memory pressure.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the environment is fully deterministic, a simple counter might suffice for reproducibility; the log is overkill and adds complexity.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent's fetch pattern is highly parallel, the ordering of log entries may be non-deterministic, undermining the audit trail's reproducibility.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The agent maintains a log of each fetch: timestamp, URL, request size, response size, status code, and whether it was a retry. The terminal state includes this log, the limits, and a hash of the agent's state. The exhaustion condition is when either limit is reached, but the log allows post-hoc analysis of which resource was the actual bottleneck. The log is structured as an array of typed events, each with a deterministic ordering.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
